findings.title: Successful time integration can consume a different physical interval from its represented timestamps
findings.mechanism: Each represented time advances one ULP=0.0001220703125, while stage equations consume nominal h=0.0001. Eight nominal increments integrate only 0.8192 of the labelled duration. Embedded error cannot identify a shared clock mismatch on constant flow.
findings.scope: Native fixed RODAS, adaptive RODAS, fixed Radau, fixed BDF, adaptive fused exponential and fixed dense RODAS. Constant autonomous scalar fixtures; no claim that every ODE or every adaptive driver fails.
findings.candidate_status: Standalone public sequential_step driver with h_eff=t_next-t passes three constant-flow origins; not installed in production, and does not resolve global cancellation, internal half steps, BDF history or adaptive max_step policy.

findings.novelty: Previously unlisted endpoint-admission counterexample on current source. The tolerant endpoint validation predates this update; not classified as an introduced regression.
findings.title: A nonzero integration span can accept a singleton output schedule and return y0 labelled as y(tf)
findings.mechanism: The epoch-scaled tolerance accepts intervals=0 in uniform and admits the singleton as both endpoints. Collector initializes y0 at schedule[0] and next_index=1, so no integrated state is stored.
findings.related_observation: A two-point schedule shifted one ULP at both ends is admitted and preserves requested labels while returning values at t0/tf; velocity8192 yields absolute timestamp/value inconsistency 1. This alias behavior is source-documented but should be explicit in the public contract or rejected.
findings.scope: Public OutputSchedule::uniform and OutputSchedule::new with fixed dense/clipped RODAS consumers. Valid exact [t0,tf] control succeeds with error2.89e-15.
findings.candidate_status: Standalone strict represented-endpoint admission rejects three invalid/aliased inputs and accepts the exact two-point control; production API compatibility choice remains open.

findings.impact: The relative tolerance claim on the original finite-input action fails; floating-point Arnoldi convergence applies to the already rounded weighted problem.
scope_limits: Extreme finite dynamic range and strongly nonnormal nilpotent operator; no claim about ordinary ODE trajectories or published campaign corruption.
The weighting-loss counter is present and visible; its omission from acceptance, not missing accounting, is the finding.
Dense loss of b0 also involves the known very-large-norm Pade limitation; the finding does not depend on assigning every dense error to weighting.
Original PHI-R1/R2/R2-POL-01 fixtures are closed, not reopened by this distinct counterexample.
findings.minimal_remediation: Propagate weighting quality into every action report/consumer and refuse original-target convergence after partial loss unless a propagated physical-output bound fits the tolerance.
acceptance_tests: Positive and negative h nilpotent fixtures return accurate representable first component or typed failure/non-convergence with no original-target invariant-subspace certification.
A=0 partial-underflow control remains explicitly classified; a conservative fail-closed first patch is acceptable.
Same rule holds for fused, prefix/incremental, dense reference and final consumers.
Previously closed R2 range and amplitude fixtures remain within their original tolerances.
